title: Simple and Compound Interest: Money That Grows on Itself

questions.question: Find the simple interest on 5000 rupees at 8 percent per annum for 3 years.
questions.rationale: SI = PRT/100 = 5000 x 8 x 3/100 = 1200 rupees. Simple interest is linear — 400 rupees every year for three years.

questions.question: The compound interest on 5000 rupees at 8 percent per annum for 2 years (compounded annually) is:
questions.rationale: A = 5000(1.08)^2 = 5000 x 1.1664 = 5832, so CI = 832 rupees. Year one adds 400; year two adds 432 = 8 percent of 5400 — interest on interest.

questions.question: The difference between compound and simple interest on a sum for 2 years at 10 percent per annum is 40 rupees. The sum is:
questions.rationale: D = P(R/100)^2 = P(0.1)^2 = 0.01P = 40, so P = 4000 rupees. The gap is exactly the interest on one year's interest.

questions.question: At what rate percent will 2000 rupees amount to 2420 rupees in 2 years at compound interest?
questions.rationale: 2420/2000 = 1.21 = (1.1)^2, so the rate is 10 percent. Extract the square root of the growth factor to read the annual multiplier.

questions.question: 10000 rupees is lent at 10 percent per annum compounded HALF-YEARLY for 1 year. The amount is:
questions.rationale: Half-yearly: rate 5 percent, two periods: 10000(1.05)^2 = 11025 rupees — 25 rupees more than annual compounding. More frequent compounding, more interest.

questions.question: A machine worth 50000 rupees depreciates at 10 percent per annum. Its value after 2 years is:
questions.rationale: V = 50000(0.9)^2 = 50000 x 0.81 = 40500 rupees. Depreciation compounds downward just as interest compounds upward.

questions.question: In how many years will a sum double itself at 12 percent per annum simple interest?
questions.rationale: To double, SI must equal P: P x 12 x T/100 = P gives T = 100/12 = 8.33 years. Under simple interest the Rule of 72-style shortcut is T = 100/R.

questions.question: A population of 20000 grows at 5 percent per annum. Its population after 2 years is:
questions.rationale: P = 20000(1.05)^2 = 20000 x 1.1025 = 22050. The second year's growth is on the enlarged base — compound growth, not 1000 + 1000.

questions.question: The simple interest on a sum for 2 years is 8 percent of the sum (total). The rate per annum is:
questions.rationale: Two years' interest totals 8 percent of P, so each year contributes 4 percent — the annual rate is 4 percent. Read carefully whether the percentage is per year or for the whole period.

questions.question: By the Rule of 72, money at 9 percent per annum compound interest doubles in approximately:
questions.rationale: 72/9 = 8 years. The rule is a quick mental approximation to the exact log-based answer of 8.04 years — remarkably close over useful ranges.
